Yidis Braised French Roast
 * Yield: 6–8 servings
 * Prep Time: 20 minutes (plus 2–24 hours dry-brining and overnight chilling)
 * Cook Time: ~2.5 to 3 hours
Ingredients
The Meat & Dry Brine
 * 1 (3 to 3.5 lb) Kosher Brick Roast, French Roast, or Underblade Chuck Roast
 * Coarse kosher salt (about 1/2 tsp per pound—lightly applied since kosher meat is already pre-salted)
The Sear, Aromatics & Deglaze
 * 1 tbsp high-smoke-point neutral oil (avocado or canola)
 * 1 to 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced
 * 1/2 cup plain water (for deglazing)
The Savory Braising Sauce
 * 3 tbsp deli or Dijon mustard
 * 1 tbsp soy sauce
 * 1.5 tbsp whiskey (bourbon, rye, or scotch)
 * 1 tsp brown sugar
 * 4–5 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
 * 1 tsp coarsely cracked black pepper
For Serving (Garnish)
 * 2–3 scallions, thinly sliced (green tops and light-green parts, kept raw)
Equipment Needed
 * Wire cooling rack + rimmed baking sheet (for dry-brining)
 * Heavy cast-iron skillet (for searing and deglazing)
 * Snug oven-safe baking dish or roasting pan (such as an 8x8 or 9x9 square baking pan)
 * Heavy-duty aluminum foil
 * Leave-in meat thermometer probe
 * Immersion blender (for finishing the gravy)
Step-by-Step Instructions
Phase 1: Dry-Brining (2 to 24 Hours Ahead)
 * Salt & Air-Dry: Sprinkle the roast lightly on both sides with coarse kosher salt. Place the meat on a wire rack set inside a rimmed sheet pan and refrigerate uncovered for at least 2 hours (and up to 24 hours) so the salt reabsorbs into the muscle fibers. (Do not add black pepper yet.)
Phase 2: Cast-Iron Sear & Sauce Setup
 * Preheat Oven: Set your oven to 300°F (targeting a true oven ambient temperature around 285°F–300°F).
 * Hard Sear: Blot both sides of the dry-brined roast bone-dry with paper towels. Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Place the roast heavily marbled/fat-seam side down first and sear undisturbed for 3.5 to 4 minutes until a deep mahogany crust forms. Flip and sear the flat underside for 3 to 3.5 minutes, plus 60 seconds on the thick edges. Remove the roast from the skillet and set aside.
 * Sweat the Onions: Lower the heat under the cast-iron skillet to medium. Toss in the sliced yellow onions and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring to coat them in the rendered beef fat and pick up the browned bits. Transfer the onions into the bottom of your oven-safe baking dish and set the seared roast right on top of the onion bed with the marbled/fat-seam side facing up.
 * Deglaze the Skillet: With the cast-iron skillet over medium-low heat, pour in the 1/2 cup plain water. Let it bubble for 30–60 seconds while scraping up every bit of dark browned beef fond from the iron with a wooden spoon or spatula, then turn off the heat.
 * Whisk & Pour the Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the 3 tbsp mustard, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1.5 tbsp whiskey, 1 tsp brown sugar, 1 tsp cracked black pepper, and 4–5 thinly sliced garlic cloves. Pour the hot deglazing water from the skillet into the bowl, stir to combine, and pour the entire mixture directly over the top of the roast. (The liquid will only come about 1/2 inch up the bottom of the pan—it will double in volume as the meat and onions release their juices.)
Phase 3: The Two-Stage Low-and-Slow Braise
 * Seal & Braise to 180°F–190°F: Insert a leave-in meat thermometer probe straight into the thickest center dome of the roast. Seal the baking dish tightly with two layers of heavy-duty aluminum foil, crimping tightly around the rims and handles so no steam escapes. Bake at 300°F for roughly 1 hour and 40 minutes to 2 hours, until the center probe reads 180°F–190°F.
 * The Collagen-Melting Hold (250°F): Once the center reaches 185°F–190°F, test the thickest part of the dome with a probe or skewer. To give the internal collagen enough time at temperature to fully unwind into gelatin without overcooking the muscle fibers, baste the top of the meat with the pan juices, keep it covered (removing the foil only for the final 10–15 minutes to set the top bark), drop the oven temperature to 250°F, and hold the roast in the 190°F–195°F internal zone for an additional 25 to 35 minutes until the probe slides into the thickest center with smooth, buttery resistance.
Phase 4: Immersion-Blended Gravy & Overnight Chill
 * Rest the Meat: Remove the pan from the oven and let the roast rest in the warm pan juices for 30 to 45 minutes. Transfer the whole, unsliced roast to a storage container.
 * Skim & Blend the Sauce: Tilt the baking pan and spoon off roughly 75% of the clear yellow fat floating on the surface of the liquid (leaving a couple of tablespoons behind for richness and gloss). Pour the remaining broth, braised onions, and sliced garlic into a saucepan or deep vessel. Simmer briskly over medium-high heat for 5–8 minutes to slightly concentrate, then puree with an immersion blender until the onions, garlic, and mustard emulsify into a thick, velvety gravy.
 * Chill Overnight: Pour the blended gravy over and around the whole roast, cover, and refrigerate overnight. Chilling solidifies the internal gelatin so the roast slices cleanly without fraying.
Phase 5: Slicing & Shabbat Lunch Rewarming
 * Slice Cold Against the Grain: Remove the cold, firm roast from the refrigerator. Check the flat underside to identify the direction of the long, parallel muscle fibers, and slice perpendicular (at a 90-degree angle) to those fibers into 3/8-inch to 1/2-inch thick slabs.
 * Shingle & Warm: Spread a layer of the blended onion-mustard gravy across the bottom of your warming pan. Shingle the cold beef slices tightly together over the gravy (keeping the slices pressed against each other prevents the cut faces from drying out), and spoon the remaining gravy over the top. Cover tightly with foil and warm on a hot plate/blech for 60 to 90 minutes before serving.
 * Garnish: Right before serving, scatter the freshly sliced raw scallions over the top.

Note: this braise still tastes extremely beefy, the sauce doesn't take over.

text:
Rice (Rice Cooker)

Makes 1 batch from 1 cup dry rice (about 3 cups cooked).

Ingredients:
1 cup rice (white or brown — see versions)
Water (1 cup for white rice, 1 1/4 cups for brown rice)
1/4 tsp salt (optional)

Instructions:
1. Rinse the rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
2. Put the rice in the rice cooker pot. Add the water for your version (white: 1 cup; brown: 1 1/4 cups) and the salt if using.
3. Close the lid and start the cooker (use the brown-rice setting for brown rice if your cooker has one). White rice takes about 20 minutes; brown rice about 45 minutes.
4. When the cooker finishes, let the rice rest, lid closed, for 10 minutes.
5. Fluff with a fork or rice paddle and serve.
note: Everyday staple Yidi asked to add for planning purposes. Versions, in the three-list format: Always: salt (optional). Versions: White (default) = 1 cup long-grain white rice + 1 cup water; Brown = 1 cup brown rice + 1 1/4 cups water. Servings: 1 (one batch = 1 cup dry rice, about 3 cups cooked). Category: Side. Kosher: pareve. Prep 5 min, cook 45 min (brown is the long version — both times are in the steps). Tags: staple, rice cooker, side.

text:
Scrambled Eggs

Ingredients:
2 eggs
1 tsp olive oil (or cooking spray)
Pinch of salt
Pinch of black pepper
1 tbsp milk (optional)
1 tbsp shredded cheese (optional)

Instructions:
1. Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt (and the milk if using), and whisk until the yolks and whites are fully combined.
2. Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
3. Pour in the eggs. Let them sit for a few seconds, then gently push them around the pan with a spatula, forming soft curds.
4. Cook 3-4 minutes, stirring gently, until just set but still soft and glossy. Add the cheese in the last minute if using.
5. Season with black pepper and serve right away.
note: Everyday staple, 1 serving. Kosher: pareve as written (oil, no cheese); milk and cheese are optional ingredients — note in the recipe that adding cheese makes it dairy. Category: Main. Tags: eggs, breakfast, lunch, quick, staple.

text:
Omelet

Ingredients:
3 eggs
1 tsp olive oil (or butter)
Pinch of salt
Pinch of black pepper

Optional fillings (use any):
1 tbsp shredded cheese
2 mushrooms, sliced
2 tbsp diced onion
2 tbsp diced bell pepper
Handful of baby spinach
1 tbsp chopped fresh herbs (parsley, chives, or dill)
2 tbsp diced tomato

Instructions:
1. Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper until fully combined.
2. Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. If using onion, pepper, or mushrooms, sauté them 2-3 minutes first and set aside.
3. Pour in the eggs and tilt the pan to coat the bottom. As the edges set, lift them gently with a spatula and tilt the pan so the runny egg flows underneath.
4. When the top is almost set, add your fillings over one half.
5. Fold the omelet in half, slide onto a plate, and serve.
note: Everyday staple, 1 serving. The fillings are optional ingredients. Kosher: pareve as written; note in the recipe that a cheese omelet is dairy. Category: Main. Tags: eggs, breakfast, lunch, quick, staple.
